query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small fraction of Pt to single‐phase fcc FeCoNi alloys will induce an ordering transformation to an L10-type structure with higher magnetocrystalline anisotropy, thereby overcoming the low coercivity limitation.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or related high-entropy alloys with high saturation magnetization but coercivities no greater than about 100 Oe.
generation.intervention: Incorporate a minor (~5 at.%) Pt addition during alloy synthesis (e.g., via sputtering), followed by a rapid thermal annealing process to promote the formation of an L10 ordered phase.
generation.conditions: Samples should be processed under conditions that maintain high configurational entropy and avoid unwanted phase segregation, with thermal treatments optimized to drive the fcc-to-L10 transformation without excessive grain growth.
generation.structural_mediator: The transition from a high-symmetry fcc phase to a lower-symmetry ordered L10 phase mediated by Pt incorporation.
generation.mechanism: Pt, due to its strong spin–orbit coupling and its ability to reduce the overall symmetry of the lattice, promotes the formation of an L10-type intermetallic phase. This enhanced ordering increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy, which in turn strengthens domain wall pinning and raises the coercive field.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline fcc alloy, the coercive field is expected to increase significantly (potentially doubling or more), while largely preserving high saturation magnetization.
generation.baseline: Coercivity values of ≤100 Oe for single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its closely related high-entropy derivatives.
generation.boundary: This intervention is effective only when the Pt content is optimized to induce L10 ordering without destabilizing the high-entropy nature of the alloy; excessive Pt or inappropriate processing may instead lead to unwanted phase separation or degraded magnetic properties.
generation.uncertainty: The precise Pt concentration and annealing protocol required to achieve the optimal L10 ordering and coercivity enhancement are not fully established, and the magnitude of the coercivity increase may vary depending on processing parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of samples: one set of FeCoNi alloys with ~5 at.% Pt addition and one control set without Pt. Both sets should be deposited under identical conditions (e.g., sputtering) and then subjected to the same rapid thermal annealing treatment aimed at promoting ordering. Structural analysis (via XRD and TEM) will verify the presence of an L10 phase in the Pt-doped samples. Magnetic measurements (VSM or SQUID) will determine coercivity and saturation magnetization at room temperature.
measurements: X-ray diffraction (XRD) to identify the fcc and L10 phases
Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) for microstructural verification of ordering
Coercive field (Hc) measurements using vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM) or SQUID magnetometry
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if (a) the Pt-doped samples do not exhibit clear signals of an L10 ordered phase relative to the control, or (b) the measured coercivity in Pt-doped samples is not statistically significantly higher than that in the undoped fcc FeCoNi samples, despite controlled processing.

cited_evidence.text: In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.

In this work, the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs were prepared by vacuum arc-melt casting. Effects of Sn content on the phase constitution and magnetic properties were studied. All the samples are composed of FCC and BCC phases, whereas some unknown phases appear with the addition of Sn. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nanoprecipitates in the BCC matrix. Moreover, the Ms increases greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases with the increasing of x for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs. The addition of Sn can obviously increase the Curie temperature of the FCC phase. The phase of alloys with a mixture of FCC and BCC will transform from FCC to BCC phase at high temperature, leading to an increase of magnetization. They can be used as new soft magnetic materials at high temperatures.

Figure 9 shows temperature dependences of magnetization for SPS-consolidated and HPT-deformed equiatomic CoCrFeNiGa HEAs. In contrast to CoCrFeNiGa0.5 the equiatomic alloy shows a higher saturation magnetization and a Tc well above 390 K. The increase in M(T) below 40 K approximately indicates the presence of an additional ferromagnetic phase with an ordering temperature of ~22 K and a magnetization which is about 2 Am2/kg, i.e., ~4.5% of the other phase (blue curve). HPT processing results in a significant decrease in the overall magnetization. The low-temperature ferromagnetic phase manifests itself more clearly, and its Curie temperature increases up to 40 K. A larger magnetic inhomogeneity of the high-Curie temperature phase is evidenced by the smoother transition to the paramagnetic state. HPT processing of the equiatomic CoCrFeNiGa HEA results in a decrease in the saturation magnetization by 34% and 55% (see Table 3) at 10 K and 300 K, respectively (Figure 10).
